title: The Cells That Help It Feel

scenes.tts: Peel away the onion, and cells still hug the nerve ending. What do they add?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Cells That Help It Feel. The inner core: flat lamellar cells wrapped around the ending. Question on screen: what do they add?
scenes.narration: Peel away the onion, and cells still hug the nerve ending. What do they add?

scenes.tts: First, the settled step. In mice, force opens a channel called Pee-ay-zo two, in the sensory axon itself.
scenes.caption: First, the settled step. In mice, force opens a channel called Piezo2, in the sensory axon itself.
scenes.visual: The axon terminal with small protrusions dotted with channels. Label: Piezo2, in the axon.
scenes.narration: First, the settled step. In mice, force opens a channel called Piezo2, in the sensory axon itself.

scenes.tts: Delete it from the wrapping cells, and touch responses stay.
scenes.visual: A gene-deletion symbol over the lamellar cells, with no channel dots drawn in them; Piezo2 dots stay in the axon, which still fires to a press. Label: non-neuronal Piezo2 deletion: responses retained.
scenes.narration: Delete it from the wrapping cells, and touch responses stay.

scenes.tts: But the wrapping cells feel force too. In duck bill corpuscles, they carry their own mechanically activated currents.
scenes.visual: A pipette on one lamellar cell in duck bill skin; a current trace appears when it is pressed.
scenes.narration: But the wrapping cells feel force too. In duck bill corpuscles, they carry their own mechanically activated currents.

scenes.tts: In duck Grandry corpuscles, the Mice-ner type, depolarizing one wrapping cell could make its fibre fire, after a variable delay.
scenes.caption: In duck Grandry corpuscles, the Meissner type, depolarizing one wrapping cell could make its fibre fire, after a variable delay.
scenes.visual: Current is injected into a lamellar cell of a duck Grandry corpuscle; after a variable delay the afferent fires a spike.
scenes.narration: In duck Grandry corpuscles, the Meissner type, depolarizing one wrapping cell could make its fibre fire, after a variable delay.

scenes.tts: In mice, switching Pa-sin-ee-an wrapping cells on with light drove the fibre.
scenes.caption: In mice, switching Pacinian wrapping cells on with light drove the fibre.
scenes.visual: Blue light falls on the lamellar cells of a mouse Pacinian corpuscle; the afferent fires in time with it. Label: Chen and colleagues, 2025.
scenes.narration: In mice, switching Pacinian wrapping cells on with light drove the fibre.

scenes.tts: Switching them off meant a vibration had to be about five times larger to be detected.
scenes.visual: A detection threshold bar grows about fivefold when the cells are silenced.
scenes.narration: Switching them off meant a vibration had to be about five times larger to be detected.

scenes.tts: So these cells contribute to detection. How they normally do it is not yet known.
scenes.visual: Label: contributes to detection; normal mechanism unknown.
scenes.narration: So these cells contribute to detection. How they normally do it is not yet known.

scenes.tts: A two hundred hertz vibration repeats every five milliseconds. In duck Grandry corpuscles, delays ran from twenty milliseconds to about nine seconds.
scenes.caption: A 200 Hz vibration repeats every 5 milliseconds. In duck Grandry corpuscles, delays ran from 20 milliseconds to about 9 seconds.
scenes.visual: A clock graphic: one 5 ms cycle of a 200 Hz sine wave, beside delay bars scattered from 20 ms to about 9 s. On screen: 20 ms to about 9 s vs a 5 ms cycle.
scenes.narration: A 200 Hz vibration repeats every 5 milliseconds. In duck Grandry corpuscles, delays ran from 20 milliseconds to about 9 seconds.

scenes.tts: Predict. Could those cells be passing on each cycle?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: one signal per cycle?
scenes.narration: Predict. Could those cells be passing on each cycle?

scenes.tts: A steady delay could shift every cycle, so delay alone cannot rule it out. But the slow, scattered firing suggests a supporting role.
scenes.visual: The delay bars scatter far beyond the 5 ms cycles. Label: steady delay = every cycle shifted; slow, variable first spikes = supporting role suggested.
scenes.narration: A steady delay could shift every cycle, so delay alone cannot rule it out. But the slow, scattered firing suggests a supporting role.

scenes.tts: Those delays followed electrical depolarization of a wrapping cell, not vibration. Passing each cycle needs a direct test. For Pa-sin-ee-an wrapping cells, the question is open.
scenes.caption: Those delays followed electrical depolarization of a wrapping cell, not vibration. Passing each cycle needs a direct test. For Pacinian wrapping cells, the question is open.
scenes.visual: Label: duck Meissner-type organ: variable first-spike latency after electrical activation; cycle following not measured. Pacinian cells: open.
scenes.narration: Those delays followed electrical depolarization of a wrapping cell, not vibration. Passing each cycle needs a direct test. For Pacinian wrapping cells, the question is open.

scenes.tts: Mice-ner corpuscles hold a surprise too. In mice, most hold two molecularly distinct nerve fibres, told apart by genetic labels.
scenes.caption: Meissner corpuscles hold a surprise too. In mice, most hold two molecularly distinct nerve fibres, told apart by genetic labels.
scenes.visual: A Meissner corpuscle in a dermal papilla with two axons in different colours coiled among the lamellar cells. Labels: Ret label, TrkB-lineage label.
scenes.narration: Meissner corpuscles hold a surprise too. In mice, most hold two molecularly distinct nerve fibres, told apart by genetic labels.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking TrkB in sensory neurons from development grew up without Mice-ner corpuscles. They needed about twice the push to detect a touch.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking TrkB in sensory neurons from development grew up without Meissner corpuscles. They needed about twice the push to detect a touch.
scenes.visual: A threshold bar doubles, from about 10 mN to about 20 mN.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking TrkB in sensory neurons from development grew up without Meissner corpuscles. They needed about twice the push to detect a touch.

scenes.tts: They still detected stronger pushes. So these corpuscles help set sensitivity, but in this experiment detection survived without them.
scenes.visual: Label: residual detection at larger forces; reduced sensitivity. Small note: developmental deletion.
scenes.narration: They still detected stronger pushes. So these corpuscles help set sensitivity, but in this experiment detection survived without them.

scenes.tts: In freely moving mice, Pa-sin-ee-an neurons fired during the mouse's own movements.
scenes.caption: In freely moving mice, Pacinian neurons fired during the mouse's own movements.
scenes.visual: A mouse moving freely on a wooden branch; spike ticks appear as it moves. Label: Turecek and Ginty, 2024.
scenes.narration: In freely moving mice, Pacinian neurons fired during the mouse's own movements.

scenes.tts: The most sensitive also answered vibrations from a tap on the branch two and a half metres away.
scenes.caption: The most sensitive also answered vibrations from a tap on the branch 2.5 metres away.
scenes.visual: Far along the branch, a tap sends a ripple toward the mouse; the most sensitive neuron fires. Label: 2.5 m, the furthest point tested.
scenes.narration: The most sensitive also answered vibrations from a tap on the branch 2.5 metres away.

scenes.tts: Two detectors of change, each a nerve ending and the cells that help it feel.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the Meissner and Pacinian corpuscles side by side, each an ending wrapped in lamellar cells.
scenes.narration: Two detectors of change, each a nerve ending and the cells that help it feel.
